reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates reactive wear protection and Ag-rich lubricating layer formation in a TiNbZr-Ag alloy, but provides no data on CoCrFeNi, Ag nanoparticle coatings, or performance above room temperature. The key premises about CoCrFeNi-Ag behavior and high-temperature stability are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Ag addition to a CoCrFeNi HEA surface can form a lubricating interfacial layer during sliding from RT to 800 °C
The Ag-rich layer reduces friction and wear by lowering shear strength and preventing metal-metal contact
Frictional heating and tribo-chemical interactions drive Ag diffusion and film coalescence
The reactive wear protection mechanism observed in TiNbZr-Ag applies to CoCrFeNi-Ag
